Surah al-Shu'ara' (The Poets)

It is Meccan, except for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the poets—the deviators follow them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 224] to the end of it, and His saying: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 197]. It has been related that these two verses were revealed at Madinah, and that his poets (ﷺ) at Madinah were Hassan, Ka'b ibn Malik and Ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with them.

Al-Dani said: It has been related with a sound chain that it was revealed concerning two poets who satirized each other in the Jahiliyyah, each of whom had a group of followers. Accordingly, the surah is entirely Meccan. End of quotation.

Al-Mahayimi said: This surah was named thus because it is特 concerned with distinguishing the Messengers from the poets, for the poet, if he is a liar, is the leader of the misguided and cannot be imagined to be guided, and if he is truthful, he cannot be imagined to fabricate against Allah, exalted is He; and this is among the greatest purposes of the Qur'an. End of quotation.

It points to the fact that the mention of the poets in it serves to show that they are far removed from prophethood, and to clear the station of the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, from what they falsely alleged of him, that he is a poet. Accordingly, the surah is entirely Meccan, in refutation of their slander.

Since the word (al-shu'ara', the poets) is general, it is permissible to take it to refer to what they related, because it includes it, not that it was revealed specifically concerning it to the exclusion of others. Its clarification, if Allah the Exalted wills, will come later. It has two hundred and twenty-seven verses. Ibn Kathir said: In the tafsir of Malik, as transmitted from him, it is called (al-Jami'ah).

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Ta Sin Mim﴾.

Regarding "Ta Sin Mim": the opinions on these opening letters were already discussed in Surah al-Baqarah, and that the majority hold they are a name of the surah. Its position is then nominative, as a predicate of an omitted subject, which is more apparent than its being nominative as a subject, or accusative by an implied verb such as "recite" or the like.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verse 2:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿These are the verses of the Book that makes things clear﴾

﴿These are the verses of the Book that makes things clear﴾. The demonstrative "tilka" (these/those) refers to the surah, and the sense of distance it carries is for magnification (tafkhim). Its place in the i'rab (grammatical analysis) is in the nominative, as a mubtada' (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is what follows it, or it is a badal (apposition) to what precedes it. By "al-Kitab" (the Book) is meant the Qur'an. By "al-Mubin" (the clear one) is meant the one whose miraculous nature, sign and proof are manifest; and it is derived from "abana," with the meaning of "baana" (to be evident), or it means the one that makes clear the truth from falsehood.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers.﴾

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself (la'allaka bakhi'un)﴾ means: killing (qatil). ﴿Yourself﴾ ... ﴿that they do not become believers﴾ means: because of their not believing. And (la'alla) is for expressing solicitude (al-ishfaq, i.e. anxious concern). That is: be concerned for yourself lest you destroy it out of grief over their not believing.

﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven﴾ meaning: compelling them to faith, forcing them to it. ﴿So that their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ meaning: submissive. [22] ﴿And this is a favour with which you reproach me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾

﴿And this is a favour with which you reproach me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ This is a refutation of his claim of having done him a favour by raising him, by showing that in reality it is a calamity. For he (Pharaoh) had taken the Children of Israel as slaves, made to serve in his affairs, subjugated to his commands, and oppressed by his tyranny. Within its meaning is a rebuke of him for his extreme arrogance, his severe harshness, and his lofty authority, behind which lies a near relief and a wondrous escape.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[26–28] ﴿He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.﴾ ﴿He said: Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 27] ﴿He said: Lord of the East and the West and whatever is between them, if you were people who understood.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 28]

﴿He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.﴾ ﴿He said: Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 27] That is: because he calls to what is contrary to what was understood from the forefathers.

﴿He said: Lord of the East and the West and whatever is between them, if you were people who understood.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 28] That is: "something" (of some kind), or: if you were among the people of intellect, you would know that the matter is as I have said. In it is an indication of the extreme clarity of the matter, such that it is not confused for one who has intellect at all, and an allusion that they are far removed from the circle of reason, and that they are the ones characterized by what they accused him of, peace be upon him, namely madness.

Note:

Some exegetes held that Pharaoh was among the deniers (al-mu'attilah), who acknowledge no Creator and recognize no object of worship (p-4611), based on his apparent words: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me.﴾ [al-Qasas: 38], and that his people did not deify anyone besides him.

Ibn Kathir said: Whoever among the people of logic claims that this is a question about the quiddity (mahiyyah) has erred. For he did not acknowledge the Maker so that he would ask about the quiddity; rather, he was apparently a complete denier of Him. End quote.

We have already noted that he (Pharaoh) was, according to sound discovery and reliable history, among the extreme idolaters, and that for him and his people there were many worshipped deities, both celestial and terrestrial.

Accordingly, the meaning of His saying: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me.﴾ [al-Qasas: 38] is: a great one obeyed; and they did not shy away from applying the title "god" (ilah) to a tyrant who dominates. So his question remains, which may be understood to follow the method of logical principle, namely seeking to grasp the essence, and his amazement at the answer, then his accusation of madness, secondly, because Moses turned from the essence to the effect. It may also be that he wanted to know Him from the aspect of His unity in the lordship which Moses claimed, and that his amazement was at what he witnessed of earnestness in the call and steadfastness upon it, and the outspoken declaration of what pains his greatness and undermines his tyranny. This is what I incline to, for the people are far from being amazed that the answer was by description (rasm) rather than by definition (hadd), since the latter is a technical term of a specific group. Yet the wording admits it and does not reject it. Many people of inquiry have relied upon it, and there is no harm in our reporting some of their subtleties concerning it.

Al-Razi said: The question with "what" (ma) is a request to define the reality of a thing. Defining the reality of a thing is either by that reality itself, or by some part of its components, or by a matter external to it, or by what is composed of the internal and external. As for defining it by itself, it is impossible, because the defined is known before the defining. If a thing were defined by itself, it would have to be known before it is known, which is impossible. As for defining it by the internal matters within it, this is impossible in the case of the Necessary Existent, because definition by internal matters is possible only if the defined is composite, and the Necessary Existent cannot be composite, because every composite is in need of each of its parts, and each of its parts is other than it; so every composite is in need of other than itself. And whatever is in need of other than itself is contingent in its essence. And every composite is contingent, so what is not contingent cannot be composite. Thus the Necessary Existent is not composite, and when it is not composite, it is impossible to define it by its parts. When these two divisions are invalidated, it is established that the quiddity of the Necessary Existent cannot be defined except by its necessary attributes and effects.

Then necessary attributes may be hidden or manifest. It is not permissible to define the quiddity by hidden attributes; rather, it must be defined by manifest attributes. And the most manifest effects of the essence of the Necessary Existent is this sensible world, namely the heavens and the earth and what is between them.

It is thus established that there is absolutely no answer to Pharaoh's saying: ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 23] except what Moses, peace be upon him, said, namely that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. As for His saying: ﴿if you are certain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 24], its meaning is: if you are certain that these sensible things are traced back to a existent Necessary Existent, then know that He cannot be defined except by what I have mentioned. For since you have conceded that these sensible things terminate in the Necessary in His essence, and it is established that the Necessary in His essence is an absolute unique one, and it is established that the absolute unique cannot be defined except by its effects, and it is established that those effects must be the most manifest of His effects and the farthest from concealment, and that is none other than the heavens and the earth and what is between them. So if you are certain of this, it is necessary for you to conclude that there is no answer to that question except this answer.

When Moses, peace be upon him, gave this true answer, Pharaoh said to those around him: ﴿Do you not listen?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 25] He said this only by way of amazement at Moses' answer, meaning: I ask him for the quiddity and the specific reality, and he answers me with the agency and the effectiveness.

The complete difficulty is that defining the quiddity by its attributes does not yield a grasp of that very quiddity, because when we say of a thing that it is that to which such-and-such necessary attribute belongs, this mentioned thing is either defined merely as being something to which that attribute belongs, or for the specificity of that quiddity to which this being-necessitated has attached. The first is impossible, for his being something to which that attribute belongs is what we made the revealer; so if the revealed were only this degree, it would follow that the thing defines itself, which is impossible. The second is impossible, because knowing that it is some thing which necessitates such-and-such attribute does not yield knowledge of the specificity of that necessitating quiddity, since in the intellect it is not impossible that differing quiddities share equal attributes. Thus it is established that definition by external description does not yield knowledge of the very reality. So his being Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them was not an answer to His saying: ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 23]. Moses, peace be upon him, answered by saying: ﴿He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.﴾ It is as though he turned from defining by the creatorship of the heavens and the earth to defining Him, exalted is He, as the Creator of us and our forefathers. This is because it is not impossible that someone should believe the heavens and the earths to be necessary in their own essences, so they are independent of a Creator and an Effector. But it is not possible for a rational person to believe of himself, his father and his forefathers, that they are necessary in their own essences, because observation shows that they came into existence after non-existence and then passed away after existence, and what is so cannot be necessary in its essence. And what is not necessary in its essence is impossible to exist except by an effector. So definition by this effect was more manifest. For this reason, Moses, peace be upon him, shifted from the first statement to it. Pharaoh then said: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 27], meaning: the intended aim of the question "what" is the request for the quiddity and the specificity of the reality, and definition by these external effects does not at all yield that specificity; so this one who claims to be a messenger is mad, who does not understand the question, let alone answer it.

Then Moses, peace be upon him, said: ﴿He said: Lord of the East and the West and whatever is between them, if you were people who understood.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 28] He turned to a third way, clearer than the second, because he meant by the East the rising of the sun and the appearance of day, and by the West the setting of the sun and the passing of day. The matter is evident that this continuous governance in its wondrous manner is accomplished only by a governor. This is what I incline to, for the people are far from being amazed that the answer was by description (rasm) rather than by definition (hadd), since the latter is a technical term of a specific group. [29–39] ﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 30] ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 31] (p-4615) ﴿So he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a clear serpent.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 32] ﴿And he drew out his hand, and suddenly it was white for the observers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 33] ﴿He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 34] ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you advise?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 35] ﴿They said, "Postpone him and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36] ﴿They will bring you every knowing magician."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 37] ﴿So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 38] ﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you gather?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 39]

﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 30] ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 31] ﴿So he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a clear serpent.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 32] ﴿And he drew out his hand, and suddenly it was white for the observers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 33] ﴿He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 34] ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you advise?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 35] ﴿They said, "Postpone him and his brother."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36]

It is recited with a hamza and without it, and both are dialectal forms. It is said "arja'tuhu" and "arjaytuhu" when you delay him. The meaning is: postpone them both and their confrontation until the time the magicians gather. ﴿And send into the cities gatherers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36] That is, police (shurtah) who will gather the magicians, that is, bring them together to you. ﴿They will bring you every knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 37] ﴿So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 38] ﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you gather?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 39] That is, to see what opposes the miracle of Musa. Wonder and bewilderment had penetrated their hearts concerning it. The interrogative is figurative, expressing urging and haste.

[29–39] ﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 30] ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 31] (p-4615) ﴿So he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a clear serpent.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 32] ﴿And he drew out his hand, and suddenly it was white for the observers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 33] ﴿He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 34] ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you advise?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 35] ﴿They said, "Postpone him and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36] ﴿They will bring you every knowing magician."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 37] ﴿So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 38] ﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you gather?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 39]

﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 30] ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 31] ﴿So he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a clear serpent.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 32] ﴿And he drew out his hand, and suddenly it was white for the observers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 33] ﴿He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 34] ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you advise?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 35] ﴿They said, "Postpone him and his brother."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36]

It is recited with a hamza and without it, and both are dialectal forms. It is said "arja'tuhu" and "arjaytuhu" when you delay him. The meaning is: postpone them both and their confrontation until the time the magicians gather. ﴿And send into the cities gatherers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 36] That is, police (shurtah) who will gather the magicians, that is, bring them together to you. ﴿They will bring you every knowing magician.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 37] ﴿So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a known day.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 38] ﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you gather?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 39] That is, to see what opposes the miracle of Musa. Wonder and bewilderment had penetrated their hearts concerning it. The interrogative is figurative, expressing urging and haste.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿Perhaps we will follow the magicians, if they are the victors.﴾ ﴿So when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh: "Will there indeed be a reward for us if we are the victors?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 41] ﴿He said: "Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 42] ﴿Moses said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 43] ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs, and said: "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are the victors."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 44] ﴿Then Moses threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsely fabricating.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 45] i.e., it swallows what they had disguised as falsehood and lies. ﴿So the magicians were cast down prostrate.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 46] i.e., on their faces, submitting to him in faith, because they knew that the like of this cannot be achieved by magic.

In this is evidence that the ultimate end of magic is deception and embellishment that makes one imagine a thing that has no reality, and [it is evidence for] thorough mastery (tabahhur) in every beneficial field, even if it is not among the religious sciences. For these magicians, through their thorough mastery of the science of magic, came to know the reality of what Moses, peace be upon him, had brought, and that it was a miracle (mu'jiza). Thus, through the increase in their knowledge, which led them to acknowledge the truth and to faith, they distinguished between the miracle and magic. This was said by al-Qadi Shihab.

(p-4617) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[47–51] ﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾ ﴿He said, "Have you believed in Him before I give you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic. So you will come to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."﴾ ﴿They said, "No harm. Indeed, we are returning to our Lord."﴾ ﴿Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we are the first of the believers.﴾

﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾ ﴿He said, "Have you believed in Him before I give you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic."﴾ Meaning: he taught you some things and not others, and that is why he overcame you. Or: he made an arrangement with you about this and you colluded upon it. He intended by this to confuse his people, so that they would not believe that they had believed with insight and manifest truth.

﴿So you will come to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾ — meaning, from two opposing sides — ﴿and I will surely crucify you all.﴾ ﴿They said, "No harm. Indeed, we are returning to our Lord."﴾ Meaning: there is no harm upon us in that; rather, there is for us in it the greatest benefit, because by your doing this and our patience under it, it is a testimony to its truth. We are returning to His reward and His mercy, so we will return to the best return, as martyrs and the fortunate. ﴿Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because﴾ — meaning, because — ﴿we are the first of the believers.﴾ Meaning: those who openly manifested faith, proclaiming the truth without dissimulation.

Then He, exalted, pointed to Moses' departure with his people from Egypt by His revelation to him. Pharaoh's permission for him to leave came after he had shown him the clear signs, then he regretted it, so the divine permission came to him, as the Exalted said:

(p-4618) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."﴾

﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."﴾ That is: travel with them by night, for when he (Pharaoh) arrives he will learn of your journey to Pharaoh; he will certainly follow you with his armies to bring you back, except that you will be ahead of him and he will not overtake you.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[53] ﴿Then Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities, gathering [the people].﴾

﴿Then Pharaoh sent﴾, that is: when he was informed of their departure by night, ﴿heralds into the cities, gathering﴾, that is: assembling his army, saying what would make the enemy seem small in the eyes of the soldiers:

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[54–58] ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band.﴾ ﴿And indeed, they are enraging us.﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are all vigilant.﴾ ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ ﴿and treasures and a noble station.﴾

﴿Indeed, these﴾ means: the Children of Israel who departed. ﴿are but a small band﴾. ﴿And indeed, they are enraging us﴾, meaning: they commit acts that anger us and distress our hearts by opposing our command and departing without our permission. ﴿And indeed, we are all vigilant﴾, meaning: against their deceit and their striving for corruption on earth. ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾ ﴿and treasures and a noble station﴾, meaning: the goodly dwellings and the splendid assemblies.

﴿Indeed, these﴾ means: the Children of Israel who departed. ﴿are but a small band﴾. ﴿And indeed, they are enraging us﴾, meaning: they commit acts that anger us and distress our hearts by opposing our command and departing without our permission. ﴿And indeed, we are all vigilant﴾, meaning: against their deceit and their striving for corruption on earth. ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾ ﴿and treasures and a noble station﴾, meaning: the goodly dwellings and the splendid assemblies.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[59] ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it.﴾

﴿Thus﴾ is a demonstrative referring to a verbal noun (maṣdar): i.e., "Like that expulsion (ikhrāj) We expelled them." It is therefore in the position of an accusative qualifier (ṣifah) of an implied verbal noun, or it is an omitted predicate (khabar), i.e., "thus it is."

Al-Shihāb (al-Khafājī) said: When the matter is taken as "thus," the purpose is to affirm and confirm it, and the clause is then parenthetical (muʿtaraḍah), like the one that follows it: ﴿and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it.﴾ Al-Shihāb said: This is a metaphor (istiʿārah); i.e., We made it their possession by way of inheritance after a time. It is as if the final outcome, since it belonged to them, made them as though they had come to possess it at the moment its owners left it.

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[60] ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾

﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾ That is: they caught up with them at the time of the rising of the sun.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[61–63] ﴿So when the two groups came in sight of each other, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are overtaken."﴾ ﴿He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 62] ﴿So We revealed to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion became like a great mountain.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 63]

﴿So when the two groups came in sight of each other﴾ means: they drew near, and each of them saw the other. ﴿The companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are overtaken"﴾ means: we will be caught. ﴿He said, "No!"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 62] means: they will not overtake you, for God has promised you deliverance from them. ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 62] means: to the path of salvation from them. ﴿So We revealed to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 63] means: he struck it, and it parted. ﴿And each portion became like a great mountain﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 63] means: each separated part of it was like a great mountain.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[69–74] ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham﴾ ﴿when he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 70] ﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 71] (p-4621) ﴿He said, "Do they hear you when you call upon them?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 72] ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 73] ﴿They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 74].

﴿And recite to them﴾, i.e., to the polytheists of the Arabs: ﴿the news of Abraham﴾ ﴿when he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 70], i.e., what is it that you call upon and turn to for refuge? He, peace be upon him, knew that they were worshippers of idols, but he asked them in order to show them that what they worship has no claim to worship whatsoever. ﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 71], i.e., we persist in worshipping them, not moving beyond them to anything else. ﴿He said, "Do they hear you when you call upon them?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 72] ﴿Or do they benefit you or harm you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 73] ﴿They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 74], i.e., like our worship, so we imitated them.

Abu al-Su'ud said: They acknowledged that these idols are entirely removed from hearing, benefit, and harm, and they were compelled to make clear that they have no support except imitation (taqlid).

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[75–81] ﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping,"﴾ ﴿"you and your forefathers, the ancestors?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 76] ﴿"Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 77] ﴿"who created me and it is He who guides me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 78] ﴿"and who feeds me and gives me drink,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 79] ﴿"and when I am ill, it is He who cures me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 80] ﴿"and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 81]

[p-4622] ﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping,"﴾ ﴿"you and your forefathers, the ancestors?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 76] ﴿"Indeed, they are enemies to me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 77] meaning: Have you seen, or have you reflected, so that you know what you and your predecessors have been worshipping? "Indeed, they are enemies to me": that is, they are objects of my hatred. ﴿Except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 77], meaning: but the Lord of the worlds is not like that; indeed, He is my Protector in this world and the Hereafter, and I do not worship other than Him. Then he gave proof of the necessity of restricting worship to Him, exalted is He, by saying: ﴿"who created me and it is He who guides me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 78], meaning: to everything that concerns me of the affairs of religion and of the world, for He, exalted is He, alone guides each to that for which it was created. The relative pronoun is an attribute of (Lord), and making it a subject with what follows as its predicate is not befitting the eloquence of the Revelation. So said Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿"and who feeds me and gives me drink,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 79], meaning: He provides for me by means of the causes He has subjected and facilitated, both heavenly and earthly. He drives the clouds, sends down water, gives life to the earth by it, and brings forth by it all kinds of fruits as provision for the servants. He sends down water that is sweet and pure, which He gives to drink to the cattle and the many humans He has created.

﴿"and when I am ill, it is He who cures me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 80], meaning: when I fall into illness, no one other than Him can cure me, by means of the causes He has decreed that lead to recovery. He attributed the illness to himself and the cure to God, exalted is He, although both are from Him, out of regard for good manners toward Him, exalted is He, by specifying the attribution of cure, which is a manifest blessing, to Him, exalted is He, as al-Khidr said: ﴿"So I wished to damage it"﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], and he said: ﴿"So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity"﴾ [al-Kahf: 82], and as the jinn said in the verse: ﴿"Is evil intended for those on earth, or does their Lord intend for them right guidance?"﴾ [al-Jinn: 10]. Also, because many causes of illness arise from a person's negligence in his food, drink, and other matters. Hence the wise said: "If most of the dead were asked, 'What is the cause of your deaths?' they would say: 'Indigestion (tukhma).'"

﴿"and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 81], for it is He who originates creation and then restores it; none other than Him can do that. If it is said that death may result from a person's negligence, and He has attributed it to Himself, what is the difference between attributing death and attributing illness in terms of what good manners require? It is answered, as in (al-Intisaf): death is known to be an inevitable decree from God, exalted is He, upon all mankind, and a general judgment that does not single anyone out, whereas illness is not so, for many who are healthy are overtaken by death. Then he gave proof of the necessity of restricting worship to Him, exalted is He, by saying: ﴿"who created me and it is He who guides me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 78], meaning: to everything that concerns me of the affairs of religion and of the world, for He, exalted is He, alone guides each to that for which it was created. The relative pronoun is an attribute of (Lord), and making it a subject with what follows as its predicate is not befitting the eloquence of the Revelation. So said Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿"and who feeds me and gives me drink,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 79], meaning: He provides for me by means of the causes He has subjected and facilitated, both heavenly and earthly. He drives the clouds, sends down water, gives life to the earth by it, and brings forth by it all kinds of fruits as provision for the servants. He sends down water that is sweet and pure, which He gives to drink to the cattle and the many humans He has created.

﴿"and when I am ill, it is He who cures me,"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 80], meaning: when I fall into illness, no one other than Him can cure me, by means of the causes He has decreed that lead to recovery. He attributed the illness to himself and the cure to God, exalted is He, although both are from Him, out of regard for good manners toward Him, exalted is He, by specifying the attribution of cure, which is a manifest blessing, to Him, exalted is He, as al-Khidr said: ﴿"So I wished to damage it"﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], and he said: ﴿"So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity"﴾ [al-Kahf: 82], and as the jinn said in the verse: ﴿"Is evil intended for those on earth, or does their Lord intend for them right guidance?"﴾ [al-Jinn: 10]. Also, because many causes of illness arise from a person's negligence in his food, drink, and other matters. Hence the wise said: "If most of the dead were asked, 'What is the cause of your deaths?' they would say: 'Indigestion (tukhma).'"

﴿"and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 81], for it is He who originates creation and then restores it; none other than Him can do that. If it is said that death may result from a person's negligence, and He has attributed it to Himself, what is the difference between attributing death and attributing illness in terms of what good manners require? It is answered, as in (al-Intisaf): death is known to be an inevitable decree from God, exalted is He, upon all mankind, and a general judgment that does not single anyone out, whereas illness is not so, for many who are healthy are overtaken by death. Thus, taking comfort in the universality of death may perhaps remove the sense of its being a trial, so it is proper in good manners to attribute it to God, exalted is He. As for illness, since it is something that befalls some people and not others, it is a definite trial. Therefore, the elevated manner of conduct toward God, exalted is He, requires that a person attribute it to himself, by reference to that cause from which he is not free. What supports this is that everything he mentioned with illness, he reported as occurring definitely and certainly, because it is something unavoidable. As for illness, since it does not necessarily occur, he attached it to the conditional particle "idha" (when), saying ﴿"and when I am ill"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 80]. It would have been possible to say "who makes me ill and then cures me," as in other places, but he did not depart from the familiar, transmitted, corresponding pattern except for this reason. End of quotation.

Abu al-Su'ud said: As for causing death, since it is among the greatest of His exclusive attributes, like giving life, both in origination and in restoration, and since all matters of the Hereafter are tied to it and to what follows it, namely resurrection, He strung them together on a single thread in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"and who will cause me to die and then bring me to life."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 81]. Moreover, death, being a means to attaining everlasting life for him, peace and blessings be upon him, is far from being something he did not desire.

[82] ﴿And the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Recompense.﴾

﴿And the One from whom I hope He will forgive my sin on the Day of Recompense.﴾ That is, the Day of Recompense (al-jaza'). His "sin" (khati'ah) is what he himself regarded as such, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and considered to be a fault in comparison with his noble station.

Abu al-Su'ud said: He (peace be upon him) mentioned this in humility toward himself and as instruction for the community, that they should avoid sins, remain cautious, and seek forgiveness for what they commit, and to atone for whatever minor sins (saghair) might occur from him, peace be upon him. It also serves as a warning to his father and his people, so that they might reflect on their own situation and realize that they are in a state of wretchedness beyond measure. For his condition, peace be upon him, despite his obedience to God Most High and his worship of Him, was at the furthest extreme, since it was of that rank. So what do you suppose of the condition of those who are immersed in disbelief and in the various kinds of sins and transgressions?

(p-4624) Linking the forgiveness of sin to the Day of Recompense, although sin is forgiven in this world, is because its effect becomes evident on that day. It also conveys a dread of that day and indicates that the recompense will take place there if He does not forgive. After he had mentioned God Most High's care for him from the beginning of his creation until his resurrection, this led him to address his Lord in intimate supplication, so he said:

Discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[83–84] "My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous. And grant me a true tongue (reputation) among the later generations." [Ash-Shu'ara: 84]

"My Lord, grant me wisdom (ḥukm)": that is, wisdom (ḥikmah), or judgment between people with truth, or prophethood, because the prophet possesses judgment (ḥukm) and wisdom (ḥikmah). "And join me with the righteous": that is, grant me success so that I may be placed in their line, so that I may be among those whom You have made a means of the reform of the world and the perfection of creation. "And grant me a true tongue among the later generations" [Ash-Shu'ara: 84]: that is, a fine remembrance after me, by which I am mentioned and in which I am followed in goodness, as He, exalted is He, said: "And We left for him among the later generations" [As-Saffat: 108], "Peace upon Ibrahim" [As-Saffat: 109], "Thus do We reward the doers of good" [As-Saffat: 110].

Al-Qutaybi said: The tongue (lisan) has been placed in the position of speech (qawl) by way of metaphor, because speech is done by it, and the Arabs have also used it as a euphemism for word (kalimah). Upon this is interpreted the saying of al-A'sha:

"Indeed, a tongue came to me by which I am not gladdened, from on high, neither wondrous nor mocking."

It is also permissible that the meaning is: "And make for me a truthful one from my offspring, who will renew the foundation of my religion and call people to what I used to call them to of monotheism (tawhid)." And this is the Prophet (ﷺ). Therefore he (ﷺ) said: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Ibrahim (ﷺ)" [the Prophet's own saying, ﷺ], so the speech is by way of an omitted modifier, that is: "one who possesses a true tongue." Or it is a metaphor by mentioning the part for the whole, because the call is by the tongue.

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[85-86] ﴿And make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾ ﴿and forgive my father, for indeed he was among those who went astray﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 86]

﴿And make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾ ﴿and forgive my father﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 86]: That is, by guiding him and granting him success in faith, as his justification indicates in His saying: ﴿for indeed he was among those who went astray﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 86], that is, [astray from] the path of truth.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: "His saying: ﴿and forgive my father﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 86], etc., is like His saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. This is something from which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, retracted, as the Exalted said: ﴿And the request of forgiveness of Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114], up to His saying. The Exalted has also cut off the connection [between Ibrahim and his father] in his seeking forgiveness for his father, when He said: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Ibrahim and those with him﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4], up to His saying: ﴿and I do not own for you [anything] from Allah at all﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4]."

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[87–89] ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾ ﴿the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, [al-Shu'ara' 26:88]﴾ ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:89]

﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾, meaning: do not inflict upon me humiliation and disgrace on that Day. ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, [al-Shu'ara' 26:88] except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart [al-Shu'ara' 26:89]﴾, meaning: a person's wealth will not protect him from the punishment of Allah, even if he offers to ransom himself with the earth filled with gold, nor will his children, however mighty they may be. The matter there is not as they were accustomed to in the world. Rather, only arriving [before Allah] with a heart free from the disease of disbelief and hypocrisy, from the blameworthy traits and the ill-omened dispositions, will benefit.

Al-Zamakhshari said: How excellent is the order in which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, arranged his speech with the polytheists. When he asked them first about what they worship, he asked as one seeking to establish a point, not as one seeking information. Then he turned against their gods and nullified their affair, by showing that they neither harm nor benefit, neither see nor hear. He also [turned against] their blind imitation of their forefathers of old, breaking it and removing it from being even a doubt, let alone a proof. Then he portrayed the question within himself, apart from them, until he extricated himself from it to the mention of Allah, mighty and exalted. He magnified His affair and enumerated His favours from the time of His creation and bringing him into existence until the time of his death, together with the mercy hoped for in the Hereafter. Then he followed that by supplicating to Him with the supplications of the sincere and imploring Him with the entreaty of those who turn back [to Allah in repentance]. Then he connected this with the mention of the Day of Resurrection, the reward and punishment of Allah, and the regret and anguish that the polytheists will feel on that Day for having been in error, and their wish to return to the world so that they might believe and obey.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that Paradise will be near the place of standing of the blessed, [p. 4627] who will look at it and rejoice that they are the ones being gathered toward it. And Hell will be exposed and uncovered for the wretched, in plain sight before them, and they will grieve that they are the ones being driven toward it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verse 90–94:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[90–94] ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous﴾ ﴿and Hellfire will be made apparent for the deviators﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 91] ﴿And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92] ﴿other than Allah? Will they help you or defend themselves?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 93] ﴿So they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 94].

﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous﴾ ﴿and Hellfire will be made apparent for the deviators﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 91]: that is, those who stray from the path of truth, which is faith and God-consciousness (taqwa). The choice of the past tense form (sigha al-madi) is to indicate the certainty of the occurrence and its being firmly established. ﴿And it will be said to them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92], as a rebuke for their polytheism: ﴿"Where is that which you used to worship﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92] ﴿other than Allah? Will they help you or defend themselves?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 93]. That is: will they repel the punishment from you, or will they repel it from themselves? For they and their gods are the fuel of the Fire. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they will be thrown into it, they [the gods]﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 94], that is, the gods, ﴿and the deviators﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 94], that is, their worshippers, for whom Hellfire has been made apparent.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Al-kabkaba is the repetition of al-kabb, which is throwing someone onto his face. The repetition is placed in the wording to correspond to repetition in meaning, as if, when he is cast into Hell, he is overturned again and again until he settles at its bottom."

The choice of the past tense form (sigha al-madi) is to indicate the certainty of the occurrence and its being firmly established. ﴿And it will be said to them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92], as a rebuke for their polytheism: ﴿"Where is that which you used to worship﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92] ﴿other than Allah? For they and their gods are the fuel of the Fire. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Al-kabkaba is the repetition of al-kabb, which is throwing someone onto his face. The repetition is placed in the wording to correspond to repetition in meaning, as if, when he is cast into Hell, he is overturned again and again until he settles at its bottom."

[99] ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals.﴾

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[100–101] ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ ﴿nor any close friend﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 100–101]

﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ ﴿nor any close friend﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 101]. That is: from among those whom we used to regard as intercessors and friends, because they used to believe that their idols were their intercessors with God. They also had friends from among the devils of mankind, yet these did not avail them anything. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

Al-Zamakhshari said: "And (al-hamim, 'close friend') derives from al-ihtimam (concern), which is attentiveness, and he is the one whom what concerns you concerns him. Or it derives from al-hamma (the inner circle), in the sense of the intimate one, and this is the particular close friend. It carries the sense of intensity and warmth, as if he becomes heated and protective, out of guarding his intimate friend, looking after him, and taking up his affairs." And this is what has been said: that he is more rare than the egg of the al-anuq (a bird deemed nearly nonexistent), and that he is a name without a referent.

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[105–111] ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 106] ﴿"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 107] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 108] ﴿"And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 110] (p-4630) ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest-born follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ This is because the denial of one is like the denial of all, due to their agreement on the foundations of the sacred laws (shara'i') (the revealed laws), which are the negation of partners and the affirmation of the Creator (al-Bari') and His unity (tawhid) (affirmation of God's oneness). Or, the plural is intended to mean the singular: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 106] ﴿"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 107] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 108] ﴿"And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 110] ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest-born follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111] They meant by this those who were of low lineage and had little share of worldly goods. For honour among them lies in wealth, property, ancestry and lineage, not in virtuous character and complete dispositions, which lead a person to recognise the truth, turn towards it, then embrace it and remain steadfast in it. Moral excellence is most found in the weak, when a sincere and trustworthy counsellor stands over them, for no wealth makes them arrogant and no status distracts them. This is part of the divine care (al-'inayah al-rabbaniyyah) for them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Thus Quraysh used to speak about the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The followers of the prophets have always been like this, until it became one of their characteristics and marks. Do you not see that Heraclius, when he asked Abu Sufyan about the followers of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said, "The weak among the people," said, "The followers of the prophets have always been like this." [105–111] ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 106] ﴿"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 107] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 108] ﴿"And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 110] (p-4630) ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest-born follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]

﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾ This is because the denial of one is like the denial of all, due to their agreement on the foundations of the sacred laws (shara'i') (the revealed laws), which are the negation of partners and the affirmation of the Creator (al-Bari') and His unity (tawhid) (affirmation of God's oneness). Or, the plural is intended to mean the singular: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 106] ﴿"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 107] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 108] ﴿"And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109] ﴿"So fear God and obey me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 110] ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest-born follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111] They meant by this those who were of low lineage and had little share of worldly goods. For honour among them lies in wealth, property, ancestry and lineage, not in virtuous character and complete dispositions, which lead a person to recognise the truth, turn towards it, then embrace it and remain steadfast in it. Moral excellence is most found in the weak, when a sincere and trustworthy counsellor stands over them, for no wealth makes them arrogant and no status distracts them. This is part of the divine care (al-'inayah al-rabbaniyyah) for them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Thus Quraysh used to speak about the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The followers of the prophets have always been like this, until it became one of their characteristics and marks. Do you not see that Heraclius, when he asked Abu Sufyan about the followers of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said, "The weak among the people," said, "The followers of the prophets have always been like this." And His saying, Exalted is He:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[112] ﴿He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾

﴿He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾ This is an answer to what was hinted at in their saying that they had not believed out of reflection and insight. That is: I am only responsible for the outward, and God takes charge of the inner realities (al-sara'ir).

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[113–118] ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could but perceive.﴾ (p-4631) ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 114] ﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 115] ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 116] ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 117] ﴿So judge between me and them with a judgment, and save me and those with me of the believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 118].

﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord﴾, meaning: their reckoning concerning their deeds is only upon my Lord, who has knowledge of their inner thoughts. ﴿If you could but perceive﴾. ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 114]. ﴿I am only a clear warner﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 115]. ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 116], meaning: those reviled or those pelted with stones. ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 117]. ﴿So judge between me and them with a judgment﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 118], meaning: decide between us according to what each of us deserves.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-fattahah is judging (al-hukumah), and al-fattah is the judge, because he opens what is closed. Just as he is called faysal (decider) because he separates disputes. In al-Tahdhib: al-fath is that you judge between a people who bring their disputes to you. Al-Ash'ar al-Ju'fi said:

Is there anyone to convey a message to Umar,
for I am independent of your arbitration.

﴿And save me and those with me of the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 118].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verses 119–128:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[119–128] ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] (p-4632) ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 122] ﴿The people of 'Ad denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 124] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 125] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 126] ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 127] ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, sporting?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128].

﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ Then ﴿We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] That is: in what We did to them there is a lesson (ibrah) and an admonition (mawizah) for those after them. ﴿But most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 122] ﴿The people of 'Ad denied﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] – and they are the people of Hud, peace be upon him – ﴿the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 124] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 125] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 126] ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 127] ﴿Do you build on every high place﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128] – that is, on every elevated place (the word ri'(ريع) is read with a kasra and with a fatha on the ra') – ﴿a landmark﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128], that is, a sign; ﴿sporting﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128], that is, by building it, not out of need for it, but merely for play, amusement, and the display of strength. For this reason He rebuked them for it, because it is a waste of time and an exhausting of bodies in pursuit of no benefit, and occupation with what they have no need of. And in being absorbed in it there is a turning away from earnest effort in work, and a diverting of wealth to other than what it was created for, namely caring for the self, the family, and the religion.

[119–128] ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] (p-4632) ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 122] ﴿The people of 'Ad denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 124] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 125] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 126] ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 127] ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, sporting?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128].

﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ Then ﴿We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 120] ﴿Indeed in that is a sign.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] That is: in what We did to them there is a lesson (ibrah) and an admonition (mawizah) for those after them. ﴿But most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 121] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 122] ﴿The people of 'Ad denied﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] – and they are the people of Hud, peace be upon him – ﴿the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 123] ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 124] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 125] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 126] ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 127] ﴿Do you build on every high place﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128] – that is, on every elevated place (the word ri'(ريع) is read with a kasra and with a fatha on the ra') – ﴿a landmark﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128], that is, a sign; ﴿sporting﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 128], that is, by building it, not out of need for it, but merely for play, amusement, and the display of strength. The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[129] ﴿And you build monuments, perhaps you will abide forever.﴾

﴿And you build monuments﴾ i.e., dwellings and palaces. ﴿Perhaps you will abide forever﴾ i.e., hoping for eternity (p-4633) in this world, indicating that their doing so is due to the narrowness of their outlook upon this world, their admiration of traces (of wealth and power), their boasting of lofty structures, and their heedlessness of the deeds of those who strive and are discerning of the outcomes, the righteous and the reformers.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verse 130:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[130] ﴿And when you strike, you strike like tyrants.﴾

﴿And when you strike, you strike like tyrants.﴾ That is: you seize with violence and severity, out of arrogance and insolence. It is said: "batasha bihi" (he seized him), meaning he took hold of him with violence and force, and grasped him with severity when overpowering him. He, peace be upon him, describes them as harsh, without mercy or compassion.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verses 131–134:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[131–134] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ ﴿And fear He who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 132] ﴿He has provided you with cattle and children,﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 133] ﴿and gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 134]

﴿So fear Allah﴾, i.e., in what I command you concerning repentance and faith: ﴿and obey me.﴾ ﴿And fear He who has provided you with what you know.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 132] ﴿He has provided you with cattle and children,﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 133] ﴿and gardens and springs.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 134] i.e., give thanks for His bounties, and through His piety, be mindful of His blessings.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[135] ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

﴿Indeed, I fear for you﴾, meaning: if you do not fulfill the obligation of giving thanks for them (the blessings): ﴿the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, meaning: in this world and in the Hereafter.

(p-4634) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[136] ﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among those who admonish."﴾

﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among those who admonish."﴾ That is: indeed, we will not desist from what we are upon.

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[137] ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the ancients.﴾

﴿This is nothing﴾ i.e., this which we are upon is nothing: ﴿but the custom of the ancients﴾ i.e., their habit. They used to adhere to it and believe in it. So we follow in their footsteps. Or, what you have brought us is nothing but the custom of the ancients; they used to take up the like of it.

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:**

[138–146] ﴿We shall not be punished.﴾ ﴿But they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 140] ﴿The Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not fear God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 143] ﴿So fear God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 144] [p-4635] ﴿And I do not ask you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 146]

﴿We shall not be punished.﴾ That is: for what we do of deeds. ﴿But they denied him, so We destroyed them.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 139] That is: with a violent wind. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 139] ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 140] ﴿The Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 141] ﴿When their brother Salih said to them: Will you not fear God?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 142] ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 143] ﴿So fear God and obey me.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 144] ﴿And I do not ask you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 145] ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 146] That is: from death, cessation, and punishment.

Al-Zamakhshari (al-Zamakhshari, the author of al-Kashshaf) said: It is possible that this is a rebuke against them being left to remain forever in their bliss, never removed from it. And it is possible that it is a reminder of the blessing in God's leaving them alone with the gardens and other things they enjoy, together with safety and ease. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in what is here﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 146] means: in that which is settled in this place of bliss. Then he explained it with his saying:

**The interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):**

﴿You are only a human being like us, so bring us a sign, if you are of the truthful.﴾ ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 156] ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 159] ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 161] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 162] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 163] ﴿And I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 165] ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 166]

﴿You are only a human being like us, so bring us a sign, if you are of the truthful.﴾ ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has a share [shirb]," [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] i.e., a portion of the water: ﴿and you have a share of water on a known day,﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] i.e., be content with your share and do not crowd her out of her share of water. ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 156] i.e., because of the greatness of what you would do wrong.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The day was described as great because the punishment descends in it, and describing the day with it is more eloquent than describing the punishment, because when a time is made great by its cause, its effect is all the more great. ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them,﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] i.e., the promised one, which was that their land was shaken with a violent quake, and a tremendous cry came upon them. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 159] ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 161] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 162] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 163] ﴿And I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 165] ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 166] i.e., exceeding the limit of wisdom in abandoning the place of tilth (ḥarth), which preserves progeny and through which the human species is preserved, and preferring what was not created for that purpose, out of greed for animal desire and in defiance of the divine order of things.

Al-Suyuti related in (al-Iklil), from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that the meaning of the verse is: "you leave its like of what is permitted." From this, it was deduced that it is permissible to have intercourse with one's wife from her rear (anal intercourse).

Others disagreed with him and used the verse as evidence for its prohibition. Its explanation, as in (al-Kashshaf) and its glosses, is that "min" (from) is either explanatory of "what He created," or partitive. What is meant is the permissible part of them, as an allusion to the fact that they used to do that with their wives. From the second meaning, the prohibition of intercourse with a woman in a place other than the prescribed one is deduced. Its explanation in (al-Intisaf) is that if "min" were explanatory, the meaning would then be a censure of them for leaving the wives. (p-4638) There is no doubt that leaving the wives is combined with approaching males. In that case, what is condemned in them would be the combination of leaving the wives and approaching males, not that leaving the wives alone is condemnable. If the matter were so, the accusative (nasb) in the second would be directed at the conjunction, and it would be either the more eloquent or the required reading. Yet the majority of reciters agreed on reading it in the nominative (raf'), and they do not agree to abandon the more eloquent reading for something that has no bearing on eloquence or even on permissibility at all. When this became clear, it became evident that this meaning is not intended. Thus "min" must be taken as partitive. Then there are two things condemned in them, each of which is independently condemned: the first is approaching males; the second is avoiding intercourse with women in the prescribed place, out of desire for intercourse with them in another place. In that case, the nominative reading is correct, since the joint meaning required by the first interpretation is lost, and each of these two great matters is independently censured. End.

Similar to this is from the subtle deductions that broaden the faculties and open doors to understanding. Yet it is possible to say that the context of the verse is one of blame directed at them, more general than what he mentioned and what others mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 159] ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 161] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 162] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 163] ﴿And I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 165] ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 166]

﴿You are only a human being like us, so bring us a sign, if you are of the truthful.﴾ ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has a share [shirb]," [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] i.e., a portion of the water: ﴿and you have a share of water on a known day,﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 155] i.e., be content with your share and do not crowd her out of her share of water. ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 156] i.e., because of the greatness of what you would do wrong.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The day was described as great because the punishment descends in it, and describing the day with it is more eloquent than describing the punishment, because when a time is made great by its cause, its effect is all the more great. ﴿But they hamstrung her, and so they became regretful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 157] ﴿So the punishment seized them,﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] i.e., the promised one, which was that their land was shaken with a violent quake, and a tremendous cry came upon them. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 158] ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 159] ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 160] ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 161] ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 162] ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 163] ﴿And I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 164] ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 165] ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 166] i.e., exceeding the limit of wisdom in abandoning the place of tilth (ḥarth), which preserves progeny and through which the human species is preserved, and preferring what was not created for that purpose, out of greed for animal desire and in defiance of the divine order of things.

Al-Suyuti related in (al-Iklil), from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that the meaning of the verse is: "you leave its like of what is permitted." From this, it was deduced that it is permissible to have intercourse with one's wife from her rear (anal intercourse).

Others disagreed with him and used the verse as evidence for its prohibition. Its explanation, as in (al-Kashshaf) and its glosses, is that "min" (from) is either explanatory of "what He created," or partitive. What is meant is the permissible part of them, as an allusion to the fact that they used to do that with their wives. From the second meaning, the prohibition of intercourse with a woman in a place other than the prescribed one is deduced. Its explanation in (al-Intisaf) is that if "min" were explanatory, the meaning would then be a censure of them for leaving the wives. (p-4638) There is no doubt that leaving the wives is combined with approaching males. In that case, what is condemned in them would be the combination of leaving the wives and approaching males, not that leaving the wives alone is condemnable. If the matter were so, the accusative (nasb) in the second would be directed at the conjunction, and it would be either the more eloquent or the required reading. Yet the majority of reciters agreed on reading it in the nominative (raf'), and they do not agree to abandon the more eloquent reading for something that has no bearing on eloquence or even on permissibility at all. When this became clear, it became evident that this meaning is not intended. Thus "min" must be taken as partitive. Then there are two things condemned in them, each of which is independently condemned: the first is approaching males; the second is avoiding intercourse with women in the prescribed place, out of desire for intercourse with them in another place. In that case, the nominative reading is correct, since the joint meaning required by the first interpretation is lost, and each of these two great matters is independently censured. End.

Similar to this is from the subtle deductions that broaden the faculties and open doors to understanding. Yet it is possible to say that the context of the verse is one of blame directed at them, more general than what he mentioned and what others mentioned. And Allah knows best.

(p-4639) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[170–172] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 172]

﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ ﴿except an old woman﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171]: she was his wife, as explained in the verses. ﴿Among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171]: meaning, it was decreed that she would be among those who remained in the punishment, because she was content with the deeds of her people.

A Latifa (subtle point):

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: It often occurs in the Qur'an, especially in this surah, that the expression shifts from a verb to a derived attributive form (sifa mushtaqqa), and then the one described by it is made one of a group. Such as Pharaoh's saying: ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 29], and their saying: ﴿It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 136], and their saying: ﴿You will surely be among those stoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 116], and His saying: ﴿I am, of your deed, among those who detest it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 168]. And His saying, exalted is He, in other places: ﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 87], and likewise: ﴿Leave us, that we may be with those who sit﴾ [al-Tawba: 86]. Its like is very numerous. The secret in this, and God knows best, is that the expression by a verb only conveys that the act occurred. As for the expression by an attributive form, then making the one described by it one of a group, it conveys an additional matter beyond the occurrence. It is that the attribute mentioned is like a mark on the one described, firmly attached to him, as if it were a nickname (laqab). And he is as if from a category that has become like a specific type known for certain base traits. This would be noticed if you said: "They were content to fall behind," for in that there would be nothing more than reporting that falling behind occurred from them, and no more.

(p-4640) Consider the context, which is His saying: ﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 87], how He attached to them a base nickname, and made them of a despicable type, known for the mark of falling behind, until it became a nickname clinging to them. This answer is general for all that comes to you of such examples, so reflect on it and assess it properly.

A Latifa (subtle point):

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: It often occurs in the Qur'an, especially in this surah, that the expression shifts from a verb to a derived attributive form (sifa mushtaqqa), and then the one described by it is made one of a group. Such as Pharaoh's saying: ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 29], and their saying: ﴿It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 136], and their saying: ﴿You will surely be among those stoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 116], and His saying: ﴿I am, of your deed, among those who detest it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 168]. And His saying, exalted is He, in other places: ﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 87], and likewise: ﴿Leave us, that we may be with those who sit﴾ [al-Tawba: 86]. Its like is very numerous. The secret in this, and God knows best, is that the expression by a verb only conveys that the act occurred. As for the expression by an attributive form, then making the one described by it one of a group, it conveys an additional matter beyond the occurrence. It is that the attribute mentioned is like a mark on the one described, firmly attached to him, as if it were a nickname (laqab). And he is as if from a category that has become like a specific type known for certain base traits. This would be noticed if you said: "They were content to fall behind," for in that there would be nothing more than reporting that falling behind occurred from them, and no more.

(p-4640) Consider the context, which is His saying: ﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 87], how He attached to them a base nickname, and made them of a despicable type, known for the mark of falling behind, until it became a nickname clinging to them. This answer is general for all that comes to you of such examples, so reflect on it and assess it properly.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 172]: meaning, We destroyed them with the most severe and dreadful destruction.

(p-4639) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[170–172] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171] ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 172]

﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them﴾ ﴿except an old woman﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171]: she was his wife, as explained in the verses. ﴿Among those who remained behind﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 171]: meaning, it was decreed that she would be among those who remained in the punishment, because she was content with the deeds of her people.
