The commentary on the words of God Most High:

[173–176] ﴿And We rained down upon them a rain, so evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers.﴾

﴿And We rained down upon them a rain﴾, meaning a great rain, unlike what was customary, by which they were destroyed: ﴿so evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers﴾. They are the people of Madyan. Whoever claims that they are two nations, to each of whom Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) was sent, is mistaken. They are one nation who dwelt in Madyan; they were attributed to it at times and, at other times, to the thicket (al-Aykah) that encompassed it, which is the many intertwined trees gathered in one place.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The correct view is that they are one nation. They are described in every context with something, and for this reason he (Shu'ayb) admonished these people and commanded them to give full measure and weight, as in the story of Madyan, "the same, with the same." This indicates that they are one nation.

Note:

Abu 'Amr said: In all the mushafs, (Laykah) is written in al-Shu'ara' and Sad, with a lam without an alif before it. In al-Hijr and Qaf it is written (al-Aykah). Accordingly, Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read it with a fathah on the lam, without a hamzah before or after it, and with the ta' in the accusative, not declined. The rest read (al-Aykatu) with the lam sukun, a hamzat al-wasl before it, a hamzat al-qat' with fathah after it, and the ta' in the genitive. Hamzah reads it in pause and in continuation according to his own method. The reading of the first group was questioned by Abu 'Ali al-Farisi and others, on the grounds that there is no basis for the fathah, because transferring the vowel of the hamzah does not require changing the case from kasrah to fathah. That is, the Arabs say of al-Ahmar "al-humru" and "lahmru." The retention of the alif and lam in (al-Aykah) throughout the rest of the Qur'an indicates, as al-Zajjaj said, that the deletion of the hamzah from it, which is the hamzat al-wasl, is in the same position as their saying "lihmr." (Laykata) was also read in the genitive as an idafah outside the seven readings. However, al-Zamakhshari said: it is the proper form. As for one who reads it in the accusative and claims that Laykah, on the pattern of Laylah, is the name of a town, this is a delusion led to by the script of the mushaf, where it appears written without an alif in this surah and in Surah Sad. There are features of the mushaf written contrary to the standard orthography; these two surahs were written according to the pronunciation of the reciter, just as grammarians write "li-anna" and "li-waliyyi" in this form to indicate the pronunciation of the lightened form. In the rest of the Qur'an it is written according to the original form. The story is one. Moreover, "Laykah" is a name that is not known. End.

(p-4642) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[182–183] ﴿Weigh with a true, straight balance.﴾ ﴿And do not deprive people of their due, nor commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 183]

﴿Weigh with a true, straight balance.﴾ That is, with a sound, upright scale. ﴿And do not deprive people of their due﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 183], that is, do not diminish their rights. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is general to every right that is established for anyone, that it must not be encroached upon; and to every property, that its owner must not be usurped of it, nor be cheated out of it, nor have it disposed of, except with his permission, in a lawful manner. ﴿Nor commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 183], that is, by killing, raiding, highway robbery, oppression, injustice, and consuming people's wealth falsely.

﴿And fear﴾ Allah: ﴿Who created you and the former generations﴾, i.e., and the former generations, those who came before them from among the creation. ﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 185] ﴿"And you are not but a human like us, and indeed we think you are among the liars"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 186], i.e., in what you claim of prophethood.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[187–188] ﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us, if you are of the truthful.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do."﴾ [al-Shu'ara’: 187–188]

﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us﴾: fragments of it. It is read "kisfan" with the sin unvowelled (sukun) and vowelled (taharruk). Both are the plural of "kisfah" (a piece). ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do"﴾ [al-Shu'ara’: 188], i.e., of disbelief and sins, and of the punishment you deserve for them, by dropping fragments or other things that He wills when your term comes. So the judgment rests with Him.

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[189] ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

﴿So they denied him﴾, meaning: they persisted in denying him and did not repent. ﴿Then the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, meaning: the punishment descended upon them, of the same kind as what they had asked for, namely the falling of the sky upon them in pieces. A cloud overshadowed them, enveloped them, darkened the atmosphere above them, and the punishment covered and surrounded them. And (al-Zullah), with a ḍammah, linguistically means that which covers, and that which envelops and conceals from above.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: He, exalted is He, mentioned the manner of their destruction in three places, each with a description suited to that context. In al-A'raf He mentioned that ﴿the earthquake seized them, so they became prostrate in their homes﴾ [al-A'raf: 91], because they had said: ﴿We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return to our religion﴾ [al-A'raf: 88], so they threatened the Prophet of Allah and those who followed him, and so ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾ [al-A'raf: 91]. In Surah Hud He said: ﴿And the Shout seized those who did wrong﴾ [Hud: 94], because they mocked the Prophet of Allah in their saying: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning one﴾ [Hud: 87]. They said that in the manner of derision and contempt. So it was fitting that a shout should come upon them to silence them, and He said: ﴿And the Shout seized those who did wrong﴾ [Hud: 94]. Here they said: ﴿Then drop upon us fragments from the sky﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 187], etc., in a manner of obstinacy and defiance. So it was fitting that He should bring upon them what they deemed unlikely to occur: ﴿Then the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them﴾. End of quotation.

Regarding the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[190-191] ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them would not be believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 191]

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, meaning: in the seizing of the disobedient in accordance with their deeds. ﴿But most of them would not be believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 191], meaning: the Victorious, Who prevails in punishing whom He wills with what He wills, the Merciful, by sending the messengers and sending down the Books, so that people will have no argument against God.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how did He repeat in this surah, at the beginning and end of every story, what He repeated? I say: each story in it is like a revelation in its own right, and in it is the same lesson as in the others. So each one of them has a right to open with what its companion opened with, and to close with what its companion closed with. And because repetition establishes the meanings in the souls and fixes them in the breasts. Do you not see that there is no way to retain knowledge except by repeating what one wishes to retain of it?

The more it is repeated, the more it is able to remain in the heart, the more firmly it is fixed in understanding, the more it is established for remembrance, and the further it is from forgetting. And because these stories have struck ears that are deaf to listening to the truth, and hearts that are sealed against contemplating it, they were reinforced with admonition and reminder, and returned to with repetition and reiteration. Perhaps that opens an ear, or unlocks a mind, or polishes an intellect whose polishing has long been neglected, or clears an understanding that the accumulation of rust has covered. And His saying, Exalted is He:

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying:**

[192–195] ﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners﴾ ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾

(p-4645) ﴿And indeed it﴾, i.e., what has been mentioned of the verses that narrate the stories related, or the Qur'an which includes them: ﴿is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., truly sent down from Him: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾, i.e., Jibril, peace be upon him: ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners﴾, i.e., joined in the row of those renowned for that noble distinction and excellent virtue, which is the divine mission of warning, removing excuses: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, i.e., clear in meaning and evident in understanding, so that it is decisive against excuse, establishing the proof, and a guide to the path. The prepositional phrase is connected to the verb (نَزَلَ) (nazala, "it descended").

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[196–197] ﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the earlier peoples.﴾ ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 197]

﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the earlier peoples﴾ — i.e., in their books. Yet he, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, had not associated with their people nor studied their books. **The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[210–213] ﴿The devils did not bring it down.﴾ ﴿It is not fitting for them, nor are they able to do it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] ﴿Indeed, they are removed far from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] ﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213]

﴿The devils did not bring it down.﴾ ﴿It is not fitting for them, nor are they able to do it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] This is a refutation of what the polytheists claimed, that the noble revelation is of the same kind as what the devils cast upon the soothsayers (kahana). This comes after establishing the truth by explaining that it was brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin, i.e., Gabriel). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, they are removed far from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212], means: from listening to the angels. ﴿...removed far﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] is because they lack the readiness to receive the outpouring (fayd) of the lights of the Truth upon them, due to the inherent corruption of their souls. Thus they are pelted and kept far from the holy lights (al-anwar al-qudsiyya) and the sublime proofs (al-baraheen al-subbuhiyya).

﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213]: punished in both abodes, with the torment of confusion of purpose, disturbance of thought, weakness of doubt, and enfeeblement of the intellect in this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿The devils did not bring it down.﴾ ﴿It is not fitting for them, nor are they able to do it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 211] This is a refutation of what the polytheists claimed, that the noble revelation is of the same kind as what the devils cast upon the soothsayers (kahana). This comes after establishing the truth by explaining that it was brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin, i.e., Gabriel). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, they are removed far from hearing it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212], means: from listening to the angels. ﴿...removed far﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 212] is because they lack the readiness to receive the outpouring (fayd) of the lights of the Truth upon them, due to the inherent corruption of their souls. Thus they are pelted and kept far from the holy lights (al-anwar al-qudsiyya) and the sublime proofs (al-baraheen al-subbuhiyya).

﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213]: punished in both abodes, with the torment of confusion of purpose, disturbance of thought, weakness of doubt, and enfeeblement of the intellect in this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verses 214–219:

The explanation of His Exalted saying:

[214–219] ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ ﴿and lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 215] ﴿But if they disobey you, say: "I am free of what you do"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 216] ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 217] ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 218] ﴿and your movement among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 219].

(p-4648) "﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾": that is, the nearest of your relatives. Indeed, nothing saves anyone from Him except faith in his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. When this was revealed to him, the Prayer and Peace of Allah be upon him said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad! O Safiyyah, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib! I have no power to benefit you against Allah in anything. Save yourselves from the Fire." (ﷺ) Ibn Kathir has expanded on the narrations reported regarding this, so refer to him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 215], meaning: soften your side toward them. It is a metaphor taken from the state of a bird, for when it wishes to descend, it lowers its wing. ﴿But if they disobey you, say: "I am free of what you do"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 216] ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 217] ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 218], meaning: from sleep to tahajjud (voluntary night prayer beyond the obligatory). ﴿and your movement among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 219], meaning: those who pray. That is, your turning about among them with standing, bowing and prostration when you lead them in prayer. In other words: He sees you alone and sees you in congregation. The description with this is a reminder to take care of the prayer at night, both in congregation and alone.

Or the meaning of the verse is: your condition is not hidden from Him, whenever you stand and turn about along with those who prostrate, in sufficiency for the matters of the religion. Or it is a metaphor for His care and protection of him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and attention to him, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes﴾ [al-Tur: 48].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 26, verse 220–222:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[220–222] ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 221] ﴿They descend upon every sinful liar.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 222].

﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ That is: of what they say and of what they intend. ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 221] That is: they descend (tatanazzalu). This is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) brought to explain the impossibility of the devils descending upon the Messenger of Allah, after their being prevented from descending with the Qur'an. ﴿They descend upon every sinful liar.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 222] That is: a liar in his speech, shifting from one matter to another in his talk, and not caring about that, because he is sinful, abounding in sin and wickedness in his deeds. Since the prophetic station is exalted above all that, it becomes clear that their descent upon him is impossible.

Al-Qashani said: Because their descent occurs only when souls are prepared to receive them, through affinity in wickedness, cunning, deceit, baseness, treachery and the rest of the vices. Whoever strips himself of the attributes of the soul, ascends to the presence of holiness, has his soul illumined by spiritual lights and the lamps of celestial meteors, and his intellect shines through connection with the higher world, then it is not possible for the devils to descend upon him, nor to snatch up the knowledge, realities and laws. For they are cut off from hearing the speech of the higher dominion, and are pelted with the meteors of holy lights. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Say: Shall I inform you?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60] is a confirmation of His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿It is not befitting for them, nor are they able to.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 211], because falsehood and sin are among the requirements of souls that are turbid, wicked, dark and base, which draw their sustenance from the devils through affinity, and which call for their casting and descent according to kinship of nature. End of quotation.

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[223–226] ﴿They cast [their] hearing, and most of them are liars﴾ ﴿And the poets—the deviators follow them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 224] ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 225] ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 226]

﴿They cast﴾ means the liars, ﴿the hearing﴾ means towards the devils and their delusions and whisperings. ﴿And most of them are liars﴾ means in what they divine and in what they relate from the devils. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And the poets—the deviators follow them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 224], it is a resumed statement (isti'naf) brought to refute what they said about the noble Qur'an, namely that it is of the kind of poetry and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a poet. This is done by describing the state of poets, which is contrary to his state, peace and blessings be upon him, after refuting their claim that it is of the kind of falsehoods that the devils cast upon the soothsayers, by what has passed of the description of their states, which are opposed to his states, peace and blessings be upon him.

The meaning is that the poets, who ride on fancies, embellishments, poetic analogies and false lies, whether they are metrical or not, are followed: that is, they are kept company and their path is taken, and among their number are the deviators, those who stray from the sunnah, not others from among the people of right guidance, those who are guided to the path of truth and who call to it. This was said by Abu al-Su'ud.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 225], it is evidence that only the deviators follow the poets, and it confirms that. That is: have you not seen that they wander, heedless of their faces, in every valley of the valleys of imagination, without stopping at any defined limit, but rather they ride every mount of falsehood, lying and idle speech? Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[227] ﴿Except for those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and defend themselves after they have been wronged. And those who have done wrong will soon know what sort of return they will be returned to.﴾

﴿Except for those who believe, do righteous deeds, and remember Allah often﴾: that is, in their poetry, such that most of it is devoted to the oneness of Allah, praising Him, wisdom, admonition, and good manners. ﴿And defend themselves﴾: that is, with their poetry against their enemy, by satirizing him, ﴿after they have been wronged﴾: that is, their satire is by way of retaliation against those who satirize them, a fitting recompense. Allah says: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾ [an-Nisa': 148], and He says: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same way as he has transgressed against you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194].

Ibn Kathir said: It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hassan: "Satirize them, or he said, satirize them, and Jibril is with you." And Imam Ahmad narrates from Ka'b ibn Malik that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed about poetry what you know; how do you view it?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand my soul is, what you shoot at them is like the spray of arrows."

Notes:

First: Al-Qasimi said in al-Iklil (The Crown): In the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the poets are followed by the misguided﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 224], there is a condemnation of poetry, and of exaggeration in praise, satire, and its other kinds, and its permissibility in asceticism, literature, and noble character, and the permissibility of satire for one who has been wronged, as a means of defense. End.

Al-Zamakhshari related from Amr ibn Ubayd that a man from the 'Alawiyyah said to him: "Indeed my chest surges with poetry." He said: "What prevents you from it in what is not objectionable?" The matter concerning it is that poetry is a branch of speech; its good is like the goodness of speech, and its bad is like the badness of speech.

Second: Ibn Ishaq mentioned that when the verse ﴿And the poets are followed by the misguided﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 224] was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) weeping. They said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." The Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ and said: "You are them."

Ibn Kathir said: However, this surah is Meccan, so how can the occasion of revelation of these verses concern the poets of the Ansar? There is room for consideration in this. Nothing has been related about it except mursal reports that cannot be relied upon. And Allah knows best. But the exception includes the Ansari poets and others, so that it includes whoever among the poets of the Jahiliyyah was engaged in disparaging Islam and its people, then repented, turned back, returned, desisted, did righteous deeds and remembered Allah often, in exchange for what preceded of evil speech. For good deeds erase bad deeds. Islam and its people were praised in place of what he used to disparage. As 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said when he embraced Islam:

"O Messenger of the Sovereign, my tongue has mended what I had torn, when I was a destroyer;
When I used to contend with Satan in the paths of error, and whoever inclines to his inclination is ruined."

Likewise Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who was among the people most hostile to the Prophet (ﷺ), for he was his cousin and the most prolific in satirizing him. When he embraced Islam, no one was more beloved to him than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would praise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). End.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who have done wrong will soon know what sort of return they will be returned to﴾ are a severe threat and a firm warning, due to what "will soon know" contains of magnifying its object, and in "those who have done wrong" of its generality and comprehensiveness, and in "what sort of return they will be returned to" of its vagueness and awesomeness, as if it were impossible to know it, though they have seen what befell them in this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
